examples.text: Ic wāt, ðæt se fisc gōd is.
examples.context: The speaker presents the quality of the fish as a known fact; indicative target.

examples.text: Hē sægð, ðæt se fisc gōd sīe.
examples.context: The narrator reports another person's assertion without separately endorsing it; subjunctive target.

examples.text: Hē sægde, ðæt se fisc gōd wǣre.
examples.context: The reported state belongs to the time of his past speech; bounded preterite-subjunctive model, no universal backshift rule.
An embedded wh-clause after knowing; selected subjunctive without asserting that every attested dependent question must have it.

examples.text: Saga mē, hwæðer ðā męnn gearwe sīen.
examples.context: A request for the answer to a yes/no question; hwæðer is invariant whether, not the agreeing which-of-two adjective.

examples.text: Se mann hēt hine ðone fisc beran.
examples.context: Accusative hine is the commanded actor; the fish is the infinitive's separate accusative object.

examples.text: Ic gesēo ðone mann ðone fisc beran.
examples.context: The observer sees the man performing the action; two accusatives have distinct functions.
Gōdne predicates a quality of the accusative object, not of the nominative subject; based on the independently audited gewyrcean frame.
The speaker is not king; a present unreal wish, not an ordinary statement about a past reign.
The finite subject is also the understood actor of the plain infinitive; compare the newly taught separate-actor command frame.
Prior naming frame, with a noun predicate; distinguish it from the command example that follows.
Command frame with the same finite morphology and actor phrase as the naming example; the infinitive marks the different construction.

compositions.title: The fisherman and his companion
compositions.text: Se fiscere and his gefēra standað on ðǣm strande. Se gefēra cwið: “Saga mē, hwæt ðū hæbbe.” Se fiscere sægð, ðæt hē męte hæbbe. Hē hǣtt his gefēran ðone fisc beran. Se gefēra birð ðone fisc. Se fiscere cwið: “Ic gesēo ðē ðone fisc beran. Nū wāt ic, ðæt ðū mē hilpst.”
compositions.scope_note: A newly composed connected exchange: request for information, report, instruction, fulfilled action and observed result. Fiscere becomes productive through the assigned Cook vocabulary; all other lexical material is already productive. The hē/his sequence continues the fisherman as the speaker/commander, while the companion carries the fish. Subjunctive hæbbe in an embedded question/report contrasts with asserted indicative hilpst after knowing. The passage does not use the still citation-only infinitive witan or the still supplied adjective geong.

audit_requests: Verify sęcgan + dative addressee + embedded wh/whether question, including Saga mē.
Verify witan + dependent wh question and selected mood within the stated scope.
Check every literal form against actual prior or explicitly new lexical records before contract.
Independent translations must be prepared without consulting the private intended translations.
